extracted.intended_audience: DoD policymakers, acquisition and contract officials, procurement analysts, and researchers interested in federal outsourcing/competitive sourcing policy
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and implementing OMB Circular A-76 requirements and FAIR Act obligations to decide whether recurring commercial activities should be performed by private contractors or federal employees, including use of managed competitions and cost-comparison studies within the Department of Defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of performance assignment for recurring commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular defines federal policy for determining whether recurring commercial activities should be transferred to performance by the private sector, or performed by federal government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply OMB Circular A-76 policy to recurring commercial activities to decide assignment of performance responsibility (private sector vs federal employees). The Circular frames this as the central test for outsourcing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act reporting and activity identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAIR Act creates statutory reporting requirements for federal executive agencies, by requiring federal executive agencies to identify activities both inherently governmental and those not inherently governmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must inventory and report activities according to the FAIR Act; this identification is a statutory step that supports outsourcing/competition decisions and governmentwide transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inherently governmental vs not inherently governmental activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal executive agencies are required to identify activities that are inherently governmental and those that are not inherently governmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishing inherently governmental activities from non-inherently governmental ones is a prerequisite to determining which functions are eligible for competitive sourcing or conversion to contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct managed competitions to determine best performer
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must conduct managed competitions to determine who is best to perform the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managed competitions (competitive sourcing competitions) are the mechanism prescribed to evaluate whether government or private-sector performance is preferable for a given activity; they determine the best performer based on comparison criteria (e.g., cost, performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive sourcing as a governmentwide management initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing, through managed competitions, was a major initiative identified by the first Bush Administration's Presidential Management Agenda, and one of five governmentwide initiatives to improve the management and performance of the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive sourcing is framed as an administration-level reform priority intended to improve efficiency and performance; agencies should view managed competitions within that broader management agenda and expect continuity of focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OMB Circular A-76 cost comparison studies
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD has set the pace as the lead federal agency in using OMB Circular A-76 cost comparison studies as a tool for managing competition for federal contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-76 cost-comparison studies are a central analytic tool for determining whether in-house or contractor performance is more cost-effective; DoD practice emphasizes their use to manage sourcing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of positions opened to managed competition in DoD
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of its Defense Reform Initiative, DOD announced that 229,000 positions would be opened to managed competition; by FY2005, some 237,000 jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates the scale and implementation expectation for competitive sourcing within DoD and serves as an operational benchmark for how extensively managed competitions may be applied across positions/functions.
